name: btor2-ind
notes: Bounded model checking that certifies what it proves: a greatest-fixpoint refinement first looks for an inductive, safe bit-invariant (state bits that never leave their initial constant) and writes it as a certificate; otherwise BMC deepens and after each proven depth the plain k-induction step is tried from an arbitrary state, the proven depths being the base for free; a closed step is written as a k-induction certificate. Failing both, the plain BMC verdict: a self-replayed witness, a bounded all(k), or an honest partial. Every certificate is {"schema": "induction", "payload": ...}, discharged by btor2@2's judge at the stop and never taken on faith; at admission all three universal corpus items discharged. Bit-vector fragment with the signed division family; arrays refused with a partial. Budgets derive from the wall argument, never the clock. Era-6 revision 1 = the Era-5 btor2-ind text re-cut with the v6 certificate envelope.
